U34 'not done' for PLAIN sources: bash gives no way to see a plain source's rc, so a plain-sourced unit counts as complete once its source frame has returned (lazily marked at the next kk.unit/kk.uses), unless a loader error happened while it was loading (a failing kk.uses called from its file scope, or a header error/cycle of a unit it sources) — that taints the innermost loading unit and a later kk.uses of it says 'not completely loaded' (rc 2) until kk.unit --forget. A plain-sourced unit failing by its own `return N` with no loader error stays undetectable (documented in kuse.sh). The literal reading (registered + not done by kk.uses = error) would make P7 / every 'test sources unit X, unit Y does kk.uses X' fail

loader messages: `kbool: error: ...` / `kbool: WARNING: ...` on stderr, printed unless VERBOSE_KKLASS=quiet (the kk.warn rule), not kk.debug: a loader error is a compile error, not a member's rc-1 miss
KK_UNIT_DIR is a plain global shell variable (not exported to the environment): it is meaningful only while a unit is being sourced in THIS shell; 'exports' in U17 read as 'provides'

kk.unit and kk.uses refuse to work (rc 2) unless kbool.sh is loaded (the [kbool] sentinel): this keeps the loader guard exact — the registry is non-empty iff kbool.sh is loaded — even when kuse.sh is sourced on its own (kklass 128, tcustomapplication do that)

kbool.sh registers the system units kuse, klib, kerr, kvar, kcfg AND itself as unit `kbool` (the sentinel, so `kk.uses kbool` is a no-op); on any failure it empties the whole registry and restores KBOOL_HOME (unset or the preset value), so the guard stays off and a retry works; KBOOL_HOME is always set to the folder kbool.sh was sourced from (a preset KBOOL_HOME pointing elsewhere is overwritten on success — config precedence is U1b)
KBOOL_HOME = the lexically normalised root only when `<normalised>/kbool.sh -ef BASH_SOURCE`, else the absolute spelled root (a symlinked `..` keeps the physical spelling)

decisions.merge_rule: scalar keys (debug, ckkdir): the strongest level that sets the key wins; an empty value counts (sets it to nothing). List keys (unitpath, defines): every level's entries, strongest level first (env KBOOL_CONFIG, project, user, system), each in file order, exact duplicates dropped — so project folders are searched before user ones and those before the system config's, the same order as U14 (caller -> project -> system). An EMPTY list value (U39, owner 2026-10-07) drops the entries above it in its own file and every weaker ENVIRONMENT level's (user, system) — never the project's lists; the project resets the inherited user/system entries with its own empty value. The built-in system paths (kkore, kklass, kcl/*) are not a config level: always searched last, never reset
decisions.unknown_keys: WARNING with file:line, the line skipped (not silent: a misspelt `unit_path` would otherwise do nothing without a trace; not an error: a config shared by two kbool versions still loads in the older one)
decisions.keys: unitpath (list, folder), defines (list, space-separated ASCII identifiers, case-sensitive), debug (quiet | default | debug; '' = default), ckkdir (folder)
decisions.kk_config_shape: kk.config KEY [OUTVAR]: scalar -> RESULT, rc 1 + RESULT='' when unset/empty; list without OUTVAR -> RESULT newline-joined; list with OUTVAR -> array + RESULT = count (kcl 1.7), rc 1 + RESULT='' + OUTVAR emptied when the list is empty; printed inside $( ) (kcl 1.1); rc 2 silent (kk.debug) for no / unknown key, OUTVAR on a scalar, a bad or reserved OUTVAR (kk._outName), extra args; rc 2 printed when kbool.sh is not loaded in this shell; an OUTVAR that is associative or readonly -> rc 2 silent; keys exact under nocasematch (kcl 1.6); kk.defined with more than one argument -> rc 2
decisions.debug_level: the config writes VERBOSE_KKLASS only when it is unset or still holds the value the config itself wrote (__KK_CFG_VKW): a VERBOSE_KKLASS from the environment (even empty) or set by the script always wins; `debug = default` after a config-written level unsets it again. Not exported (a child re-reads the config levels itself); under `set -a` the config-written value is `export -n`-ed (R7a); LIMITATION (R7b): a script that assigns exactly the value the config wrote cannot be told from it, so a later kk.project may change it
decisions.kk_project_relative_path: a relative PATH is relative to the CALLING file's folder ($PWD at a prompt), like kk.uses PATH (U12); NAME = no `/` or `\` and not ending in `.conf`; `.` and `..` refused
decisions.U37_scope: kk.project is refused after the first use of a non-system unit: any kk.uses argument that is a path or a name kbool.sh did not load (found or not, failing or not) AND any unit registered by kk.unit (a plain source) — a plain-sourced unit could have consulted kk.defined or resolved names without the project. kbool.sh clears the flag after its system units (future-proof for U3, when they register through kk.unit); a unit kbool.sh loaded, named by its PATH, is that unit (no-op, kk.project stays open — R9a)
decisions.second_kk_project: owner 2026-10-07 (R9c): the SAME file (string or -ef, any spelling) -> rc 0 no-op, like kk.uses, also after units were used; another file -> rc 2 naming the project already set
decisions.registry_less_child: kk.project bootstraps $KBOOL_HOME/kbool.sh first (like kk.uses, R8); kk.config and kk.defined refuse with rc 2 (queries, like U1a's kk.defined)
decisions.test_hook: __KK_CFG_ETC replaces /etc/kbool (read from the environment, never assigned) so tests never read a real /etc/kbool; HOME/USERPROFILE/ProgramData are plain env overrides
decisions.file_format: UTF-8 (a leading BOM is skipped), LF or CRLF; UTF-16 (FF FE / FE FF), any NUL byte, or CR-only line ends -> ONE WARNING and the whole file ignored; lines over 4096 characters -> WARNING file:line, skipped; files over 64 KiB -> WARNING, read to the limit, the cut last line dropped; a define line with non-names -> ONE WARNING listing them, the names on it kept

pattern.1_header: line 1 `#!/bin/bash`; lines 2-3 EXACTLY the §7.4 relative header: `[[ ${__KK_UNITS[@]@a} == A* ]] || source "${BASH_SOURCE%U.sh}../../kbool.sh" || return` and `kk.unit U || return $__kk_unit_rc` (U = the file stem); then the unit's own comment block, unchanged. pattern.2_guard: the hand-written guard block is DELETED with its comment lines (`# Re-source guard ...` + `if [[ -n "${_U_SOURCED:-}" ]]; then return; fi` + `declare -g _U_SOURCED=1`); nothing replaces it — the header is the guard
pattern.3_dependencies: the pair `U_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"` + `source "$U_DIR/../../kklass/kklass_pascal.sh"` (and its `# Source the kklass ...` comment) is replaced IN PLACE — same position, e.g. after the locale self-heal, so the load order of the unit's own statements is unchanged — by the note (4 comment lines, verbatim: `# A unit (kklass/USES_PLAN.md §7.4, phase U4): the two header lines at the` / `# top load kbool.sh when needed and make a repeated \`source\` a no-op, also` / `# under \`set -eu\` (they replaced the D7 re-source guard). Dependencies come` / `# through kk.uses.`) and `kk.uses kklass_pascal || return` (or `kk.uses kklass` / `kk.uses kklass_decl` — whatever module the old path named). Other kcl units by NAME on further `kk.uses NAME || return` lines (one name per line, in the old source order): `source "$U_DIR/../tpath/tpath.sh"` -> `kk.uses tpath || return`. No kkore module is ever named (kbool.sh loads them all, U1). An OPTIONAL dependency the unit handles itself: `kk.uses --optional X || fallback` (U42)
pattern.4_namespaces: census: every function defined at file scope (column 0) as `X.name()` whose X is neither a class of the unit (`class X`, `defineClass X`, `declareClass X`) nor the unit name -> X is a helper namespace: `kk.namespace X [Y ...] || return` on the line right after the kk.uses line(s), preceded by the 2 comment lines `# X.* are this unit's shared helpers, not a class: a declared` / `# function namespace (U40), so no class or instance may take that name.` (several: `# X.* and Y.* are ...`). The unit's own name needs no line (kk.unit declares it); a class that bears the unit's name (tpath, dateutils) is the U40 owner exemption
pattern.5_runtime_dir: U_DIR is dropped when it only served the source line (all of G1). pattern.6_other_code: no other change in the unit: no reflow, no fixes; `set -eu` sourceability holds (the header is set -u/-e safe, a re-source returns 0)
pattern.7_tests: REPLACED in G1 review round 1 (R3-R5): (a) add the unit's row to kcl/tests/kcl_units.sh KCL_UNITS (UNIT|NAMESPACES|FLAGS|DIR; FLAGS rundir / readonly; DIR only when the file is not kcl/UNIT/UNIT.sh); (b) add its runtime stub kcl/tests/NNN_<UNIT>.sh — a copy of 101_tstopwatch.sh, the unit is the file name's stem after NNN_ (G1 101-107; G2 2NN, G3 3NN, G4 4NN, G5 5NN); 001 fails while a row has no stub or a stub no row. 001 checks every row statically (header lines 2-3, no old guard `*_U_SOURCED` / `U_DIR` / `u_DIR` / hard path / fork / source statement, `kk.uses NAME... || return` form, `kk.namespace X... || return` form and place, static census, lint); the stub runs kclt_unit_tests: once (one set -eu process in a private counting tree), name (runtime census through compgen -A function before/after, owners, old variables through compgen -v), taken, nsbad (rows with namespaces).
